properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Seneca Resources Co Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-03-01
Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 843313
Permit API: 047-24947
Unconventional: Yes
County: Elk
Municipality: Jones Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-03-01
Comments: At 10 am, I received a call from Seneca Resources stating that a snow plowing operator had struck a line containing production water on the E08-L pad and allowed approximately 110 gallons of fluid to drain to the ground. I arrived on site at approximately 1030 am and the operator had a vac truck on site to remove free fluid. A snow plow operator struck the line running from the production water tanks to frac tanks at approximately 815 am, severing it and allowing production water to flow out. They were not actively pumping water at the time, so the estimated volume is lower. The area showed melted snow and some free liquid, approximately 10 ft x 15 feet in size. Conductivity readings were >20,000 µs/cm on the Department issued meter and approximately 107,000 µs/cm on Seneca's meter. No fluid was flowing off site, due to the snow pack on location. The Operator was in the process of getting a container to the site which would allow for removal of any impacted soil. Further inspection will be done as necessary.

Comments: On 07/24/2024 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Southwestern's (SWN's) Vanorder-Patrick (12 Pad) Well Pad in Herrick Township, Bradford County. The weather was 70 degrees and cloudy. Rain fell on the pad within the last24 hours. I arrived at 1035 hours. The site remains stabilized with greater than 70% perennial vegetative cover. There was no accelerated erosion or sedimentation observed. There are two post-construction stormwater management structures onsite. They appear to be functioning properly. Pooled water on the pad was field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) between 192.8-262 us/cm. There was no evidence of any spills or releases. There was one produced fluid tank held within secondary containment onsite. There were nine gas processing units (GPUs) held within secondary containment onsite. There were nine wells capable of producing. There were each properly tagged with the American Petroleum Institute (API) identification numbers. There were numerous temporary storage tanks held within secondary containment onsite. Violations remain outstanding at this site from a previous release. Site remediation has been performed and a Remediation Action Completion Report has been submitted to DEPs Environmental Cleanups and Brownfields program for review. The outstanding violations will be closed once attainment with Act 2 standards has be confirmed.The DEP recommends:1. Disposing of stormwater held in the secondary containment structures as soon as possible to maintain compliance with 25 PA 78a64a(e).I departed at 1135 hours.

Violation ID: 906420
Permit API: 015-23632
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Tuscarora Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 2/01/2021
Comments: On 02/01/2021, DEP representative John Ciccone conducted an administrative report for Chesapeake Appalachia LLC's (CALLC) STONE BRA location. This location is currently in flowback operations after fracking the STONE N 3HC and STONE N 104HC wells. This report is in response to a spill notification (CTS # 354624) received on 01/30/2021 at 0900 hours. The purpose of this report is to document details regarding the reported release, remediation actions taken thus far by CALLC, and to cite violations. On 01/30/2021, Tony Savitski (CALLC) reported that at 0900 hours, a mixture of rainwater and produced water spilled to the pad surface due to a hole in a containment structure. An estimated 42 gallons was reported as released. An estimated 20' x 20' area of impacted soils has been excavated and stored on containment, pending sample results for proper disposal. It was reported that no fluid escaped from the pad. On 02/01/2021, I contacted Eric Hottenstein (CALLC) at 0845 hours in order to gather more details regarding the release. Mr. Hottenstein stated that a frac tank storing produced fluids and stationed within secondary containment leaked fluid into containment. A hole in containment, believed to be caused by a hose puncture, resulted in the mixture of rainwater and produced fluid to leak to the pad surface. Mr. Hottenstein estimated that approximately 10 tons of impacted soils had been excavated and stored in containment. Mr. Hottenstein stated CALLC plans to pursue ACT 2 remediation. Samples for ACT 2 purposes have been collected and the frac tank containment has reportedly been fixed. Photos of the site have been forwarded by Mr. Hottenstein and attached to this report. The release of 42 gallons of the rainwater and produced fluid is in violation of Pa. Code 78a.56(a), CSL 402(b), and SWMA 301. Due to the quantity of the reported release, it is requested that CALLC refer to and remediate in accordance with Pa. Code 78a.66. This release is referred to the DEP's Bureau of Environmental Cleanups and Brownfields.

Report Details

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8184782
Permit API: 125-22544
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: Somerset Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/25/2024
Comments: On April 25, 2024, inspection conducted at the US Natural Resources 1-P085 well site in Somerset Township, Washington County. This inspection follows up to IR 3744557, which documents the Department's response to a spill that reportedly occurred on April 10, 2024, when the onsite brine tank overfilled with production fluid and pushed a grease-like layer sitting on top of this fluid out the top of the tank onto the ground below. Present at this inspection were KPI representative Joel Grecko and myself. Mr. Grecko reports that remediation of the impacted area was completed on April 16, 2024. The following was observed:The access road appeared to be stable at the time of inspection with no observed evidence of accelerated erosion or sedimentation (see photo 1). Tire rutting was observed in the well site at the time of inspection (see photo 2). The area impacted by the grease-like substance was excavated with no staining observed in this area (see photo 3). No elevated soil conductivity was detected in this area, underneath the brine tank valve, or within the majority of the earthen berm surrounding the brine tank (see photos 4, 6, 7, 8, and 9). An area of slightly elevated conductivity was detected in the southwestern corner of the earthen berm surrounding the brine tank (see photos 5 and 9). However, no staining, distressed vegetation, or other visual impacts were observed in this area. The well head was equipped with a well tag, and no staining or distressed vegetation was observed on the ground around it (see photos 10 and 11). The operator's information was posted on the meter box (see photo 13). The brine tank appeared to be sound at the time of inspection, with any remaining grease-like substances appearing to have wiped off (see photo 14). Mr. Grecko was conducting brush clearing onsite when the Department arrived. Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends that maintenance is conducted on the well site (and on the access road, if needed) now that remediation is complete to address the aforementioned tire rutting. The Department recommends that the operator assess and evaluate the area of elevated conductivity in the earthen berm, as the conductivity reading taken in this location is an outlier when compared to other soil conductivity readings taken onsite. Finally the Department recommends that the remediated area is mulched and seeded until 70 percent vegetative growth coverage is achieved. The Department requests a response to this inspection report from the operator with the waste manifest from remediation included in this response, when available.Violations shall be noted and immediately corrected.

Comments: On 03/26/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Fowler Well Site following routine complete inspections that were conducted for each well on 01/03/2024 (See IR 3670374 for example). I was accompanied by Environmental Trainee Olivia Holley (PA DEP). It was noted that sediment was being transported towards the main township road, Little Daniel's Run Road, down the side of the road to a storm grate. Sediment was accumulating within the rock lined channel and pooling at the base of the channel, adjacent to the access road.It was discussed with EQT via phone for plans to install a rubber belting water bar to divert the spring water towards the rock lined channel instead of flowing down the center of the access road. EQT also used dust suppressant on the road. The following was observed during inspection on 03/26/2024:The rubber belting water bar was not yet installed on the access road. The access road displayed some dust suppressant, however I recommend that additional is applied, focusing on the beginning of the access road where the spring is out letting and the water is leaving the site. There was a section of dust suppressant at the top of the road near the tanks, however it was unclear if this area was existing (Photos 1-6).Newly installed storm grate at the base of the rock lined channel was in generally good condition. Some sediment accumulation noted on the bottom. No sediment noted within stone around the storm grate coming from the stabilized bank or the channel (Photos 7, 8).Sediment was accumulating along the base of the access road and main township road which appeared to be originating from the site. This sediment was leading towards the storm grate along the main township road. Sediment did not appear to be accumulating within the storm grate (Photos 9-12).Sediment laden water leaving the access road was noted leading towards the township storm grate. Some rills were noted within the sediment (Photos 13-18).The channel on the property across the street where the township storm grate and culvert outlets did not appear to be accumulating sediment from the access road (Photo 19). Overview of access road, storm grates and outlet across the street leading to Little Daniels Run (Photo 20).Due to the continuing discharge of sediment laden water off of the access road and sediment accumulation of sediment along the main township road, violations of 102.4(b)1, 102.11(a), and 78a.53 are being issued.

Report Details

Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 924086
Permit API: 129-26518
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Penn Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/19/2021
Comments: On July 19, 2021, I conducted an inspection of the Lamacz 1 oil and gas well in Penn Township, Westmoreland County. The inspection was conducted in response to a reportable release received on 7/19/2021. On 7/19/2021, the Operator reported that a landowner hit a valve while mowing on Friday July 16, 2021 and did not notify the Operator emergency number. The Operator located the voice mail on 7/19/2021 and responded immediately. I spoke with Marc Jacobs regarding the release. Mr. Jacobs indicated that approximately 40 barrels of fluid was lost from the brine tank. Additionally, Mike Walor Woodard & Curran was contracted to evaluate and remediate the impacted area. Mr. Walor indicated that the impacted material would be remediated in accordance with the Act 2 standards. At the time of inspection, The Operator was removing fluid from the fiberglass brine tank with a vac truck. I observed a significant amount of crude oil and brine spilled to the ground and resulted in a flow path approximately 500’ down gradient from the well through the landowners mowed field. The spill appeared to emanate at or near the brine tank valve. I spoke with the landowner, who admitted to hitting the valve with the mower deck on Friday July 16, 2021. The landowner also indicated that it was raining when the valve was struck. The impacted material was not observed in or appeared to have entered waters of the commonwealth. In addition to the spill, the fiberglass brine tank appeared to have been previously leaking and repaired prior to the release. A vertical dark stripe was visible on the side of the fiberglass below what appeared to be two fiberglass patches applied to the brine tank. The Department is seeking clarification on when the patches were applied and why the patched were needed. I recommend that the Operator design, construct, maintain, and reasonably protect the brine tank from unauthorized acts of third parties. The fluid lost also appears to be crude oil. The Department is seeking clarification in regard to the amount of crude oil contained within the brine tank as the brine tank was not equipped with secondary containment. Violations are being issued based on the observations made during this inspection. Additional violations maybe forthcoming pending further investigation.

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 955458
Permit API: 105-21845
Unconventional: Yes
County: Potter
Municipality: Keating Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/11/2022
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an INCIDENT inspection of the PGE – Hancock Pad A located in Keating Twp, Potter Co. on 5/12/22 @1210 hours in response to a reported release of approximately 10 barrels of brine to the pad surface (CID#364034). The weather was 73 degrees, sunny, winds ENE@3mph. Mr. Chad Earley, PGE HSE Supervisor and Mr. Matt Covine, PGE Completions Consultant were present onsite for the inspection. Mr. Earley stated a cement truck was parked in secondary containment yesterday during the previous days plugging activities. A brine solution was spilled into the secondary containment from the truck. At the end of yesteday’s plugging activities, the secondary containment was "almost full" of the brine solution. The brine solution was left in the secondary containment overnight. Mr. Earley stated when Mr. Covine arrived onsite the next morning, there was less brine solution in the secondary containment and visible staining and fluid on the pad surface. Mr. Earley estimates 10 barrels of fluid was released to the pad surface. I screened the fluid remaining in the secondary containment with an Oakton Multiparameter meter. The field conductivity was measured at 18.8mS/cm. Damp areas around the secondary containment were screened with a Groline soil conductivity meter and found to be >4.0mS/cm. Two vac trucks arrived onsite to remove the fluid remaining in the secondary containment as well as the brine solution remaining in the two water tanks adjacent to the spill area. The secondary containment responsible for the release was lifted with a telehandler and the underside examined. The Secondary containment appeared to have a seam that was not properly sealed, this allowed fluid to leak from the bottom of the containment. The visibly impacted area was estimated to cover ~20’ long x 12’ wide. As material was excavated and placed into a lined rolloff waste container, a clay layer was encountered approximately 14" below the pad surface. Mr. Earley screened the clay material with a field conductivity meter and found the material measured <500uS/cm. Mr. Earley stated the clay later appeared to be a barrier for further infiltration of the brine solution. Mr. Earley also stated the brine solution appeared to have laterally migrated under the brine tank containment adjacent to the excavated spill area. Mr. Earley stated their plan was to excavate the 12’ x 20’ impacted area, while field screening, to ensure all impacted areas are identified. PGE would then line the area with plastic and backfill with clean gravel to accommodate completion of the plugging activity. Mr. Earley stated PGE would then have the tanks and their containment removed to further screen the area under the tanks and remove any additional impacted material. I requested Mr. Earley email me pictures of today's completed cleanup activities and provided my contact information. Due to the reported volume of the release being greater than 42 gallons the operator must demonstrate attainment of one or more of the standards established by Act 2 and Chapter 250. This incident is referred to the DEP Cleanups Program for Follow-up. Violations of the following regulations are cited against the Hancock Pad A 2741 Well (API#105-21845) at this time: 25 Pa Code 78a.64(b) 25 Pa Code 78a.64(f) CSL 402(b) SWMA 301 I departed the site at 1440 hours.

Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72-hr (Stepped) pressure build-up tests, (SPBUT) being performed on all (6) wells on the Aukema pad. The Aukema 3H, 4H, 7H, 1HC, 2HC and the 101HC wells. These tests are being performed to assess the results of the initial remedial deployment of Renegades localized casing expansion tool in the production casing of the Aukema 1HC and 101HC wells on 5/17/21 and 5/18/21 and the 3H and 2HC between 1/24 - 27/21. This is the third round of testing since initial remedial work was performed. Craig Shores and Zach Burnett and Creston Consultant Reps., Will Dolan and Jason Rajan. Starting at approx. 10:00, ending annuli pressures were checked using a Digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter. Creston Consultants collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. CALLC will share gas sample results with The Department when received. Ending pressures, gas checks and time of gas sample collections are listed below for all the Aukema Pad wells. - Aukema 3H (20x13): 0.0 psi.; 0% CH4; No sample taken (13x9): 0.0psi.; 90% CH4; Sample taken @ 11:30 (9x5): 220 psi.; 95% CH4; Sample taken@ 11:35 ** - Aukema 4H (20x13): 8 psi.; 78% CH4; Sample taken @ 10:55 (13x9): 0.0 psi..; 0% CH4; No sample taken (9x5): 0.0 psi.; 46% CH4; Sample taken @ 11:05 - Aukema 7H (20x13): 0.0 psi.; 0% CH4; No Sample taken (13x9): 5 psi.; 75% CH4; Sample taken @ 11:50 (9x5): 15 psi.; 65% CH4; Sample taken @ 11:55 - Aukema 1HC (20x13): 0.0 psi.; 0% CH4; No sample taken (13x9): 79 psi.; 96% CH4; Sample taken @ 10:30 (9x5): 25 psi.; 94% CH4; Sample taken @ 10:35 - Aukema 2HC (20x13): 0.0 psi.; 0% CH4; No sample taken (13x9): 4 psi.; 87% CH4; Sample taken @ 11:15 (9x5): 314 psi.; 91% CH4; Sample taken @ 11:25 - Aukema 101HC (20x13): 0.0 psi.; 0% CH4; No sample taken (13x9): 0 psi.; 97% CH4; Sample taken @ 10:15 (9x5): 29 psi.; 97% CH4; Sample taken @ 10:20 ** The cellar floor of the 4H had a slight bubbling, an ALTAIR 5X gas meter (cal. 4/5/22) was used to screen the bubbling, 55% LEL was detected. The bubbling dissipated when the (20x13) annulus was returned to venting via Sentry valve. - The 1HC, 2HC, 4H, 7H and the 101HC had water in the cellars, but below conductor casing. The 3H had water above the conductor casing. Comments: This conventional well is equipped for production with a pump jack. A sign containing the API number, well name, and operator information was posted on a stake near the well. This inspection was conducted in response to a phone call from JR McLaughlin, a representative from Bull Run Resources, reporting a minor leak which had occurred at Well M22. Upon arrival to the site, it was evident that crude oil had recently leaked from a faulty line near the well head. The discharged crude oil remained on the well site. It is estimated that less than 1 barrel of crude oil has been released as part of this incident. No waterways have been affected from the event.The broken line had already been repaired before arriving to the site. Several workers from Bull Run Resources were actively shoveling contaminated soil and snow to be removed from the site. An excavator had been used to scrape the ground surface where the crude oil had discharged. The excavated area was seeded and mulched upon arrival to the site. Given there is no ongoing discharge and the impacted area appears to have been sufficiently remediated, the violations associated with this incident are considered corrected. A future inspection will be conducted to ensure that the initial remediation efforts were sufficient.

Comments: On 4/09/2026, the Department conducted a routine complete inspection of Diversified's Clemmer 6 plugged well site located in Springhill Township, Westmoreland County.According to Department records, this well was plugged on 4/16/2025. Therefore the well site restoration was due by 1/16/2026. A Well Site Restoration Report (WSRR) was due by 3/17/2026. A Well Site Extension Request submitted by the operator on 12/19/2025 was returned by the Department (IR 4125309). No WSRR has been received to-date from the operator for this site. A COA was entered into between the Department and Diversified on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, Diversified is to restore the Well Site in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S.A. 3216.The following was observed during the inspection:The former site access road is entirely unvegetated and appears to be used to access an active construction zone for a residential home. The plugged well site has not yet achieved 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth coverage. No evidence of accelerated erosion and sedimentation was observed on site during this inspection. However, no temporary Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) controls were observed on site during this inspection. The mailbox containing the site E and S/Restoration plans was not found during this inspection. A metal pole appears to be marking the approximate coordinate location of the plugged well. No surface fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the approximate location of the plugged well.Based on observations from this inspection, the well site and access road are not restored. The Department recommended in IR 4125309 that the Operator fully restore the well site and access road or submit a signed and completed Post-Plugging Landowner Waiver of Well Site Restoration. However, no Post-Plugging WSRR or Post-Plugging Landowner Waiver has been received from the operator. Therefore, a violation shall be issued in IR 4176643 for failure to restore the well site 9 months post-plugging, in accordance with the 3/07/2019 CO and A. Violations shall be issued in this inspection for failure to have the site E and S/Restoration plan available and for failure to install temporary Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) controls on site.

Comments: On April 28, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Chabal 2 well site in Upper Burrell Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3966229 where violations issued from IR 3965337 were left outstanding, as the start of remediation was postponed to the day of this inspection due to forecasted inclement weather. No impacts to the Waters of the Commonwealth were observed during the time of IR 3966229, and the impacted area was covered with plastic sheeting in preparation for the weather.The following was observed:The well head is equipped with a well tag appears to be free of fluid leaks at the time of inspection (see photos 2 and 3). The operator's information is posted on the separator (see photo 4). The body of the brine tank appears to be sound at the time of inspection (see photos 5). What appears to be a covered excavation stockpile was observed onsite, which may be from remediation work that has been conducted thus far (see photo 6). The path of brown staining that was observed traveling downslope from the brine tank during the time of IR 3965337 remains covered with plastic sheeting, and appears to have been excavated near the brine tank (see photos 7, 8, and 11). A soil conductivity reading was taken adjacent to the brine tank where it appears that impacted material was removed (see photo 9). Although the soil conductivity in this location did not appear to be elevated above that of the surrounding soil, some staining remained on the conductivity meter (see photo 10). Therefore it appears that additional excavation may be necessary in this location. Oil absorbent booms remain placed downslope of the covered impacted area (see photos 12 and 13). No evidence of visual impacts and/or elevated conductivity were detected down slope of impacted area (see photos 14 and 15).Based on observations from this inspection, it appears that remediation work has begun and the impacted area remains adequately protected to mitigate risk of the impact being spread by stormwater. However, the Department recommends that the operator assess and evaluate the excavated area adjacent to the brine tank for any additional remediation that may be needed.Violations issued from IR 3965337 shall remain outstanding.

Comments: Requested response for violations issued on 2/10/2021 received by email on February 25, 2021. Response shown in attached photo and will be uploaded into file. Upon review of information submitted and the inspection of the well, the well does not meet the requirements of 3214(a)(1) and 3214(a)(2). Information is being forward for additional review.

Comments: The Department conducted an inspection of the Leatherwood LLC, Stockdale #1 conventional gas well on December 14, 2022. A tag with the permit number is affixed to the well. A closed top frac tank is on site. A 2" steel line is connected to the top of the 4 1/2" production casing. The 2" steel line extends from the well to an access hatch on top of the frac tank. Based on the position of the wellhead valve, the well appears to be venting into the frac tank. Fluid is visible in the bottom of the frac tank. The volume of fluid in the tank could not be determined. At the access hatch on top of the frac tank, methane was detected. 140 ppm methane was detected at the open access hole. 17% methane and 268 ppm carbon monoxide was detected at the open end of the 2" steel line in the frac tank. No methane gas was detected at or around the well. No leaks or odors were observed or noted at or around the well. The production annulus is shut in. The well is not equipped for production. The Department received a well record for the Stockdale 1 on 11/12/2021. According to the well record, drilling was completed on 10/13/2021. Based on the Departments records, a completion report has not been submitted. The Department contacted the operator regarding the status of the well. According to the operator, the well was stimulated on 11/2/2021 and 8/11/2022 and additional work may be required to complete the well. The Department informed the operator of the regulatory timeline and requirements for submittal of a completion report after the completion of a well.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 7/11/2023
Comments: On July 11, 2023, inspection conducted at the Rumpelstiltskin well pad in Somerset Township, Washington County. Present were myself, EQT representatives David Crayne and Carey Vallor-Bell, and Moody representative Jona Stoskey. This inspection was conducted in response to a spill that reportedly occurred on July 10, 2023 at 2:35 PM, and was reported to the Department the same day at 4:27 PM by DJ Hardy. The Department spoke over the phone with Mr. Hardy while en route to the pad, who explained that a GPU dumpline failed and spilled approximately one barrel of brine fluid onto the ground. He also stated that the area behind the unit was excavated, but impacted soil remains around and under it. The following was observed:At the time of inspection, the Act 9 sign was installed at the entrance of the access road and was not obstructed from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). The ERP was onsite (see photo 2). The access road and well pad appeared to be stable with no evidence of accelerated erosion or sedimentation (see photos 3 and 4). GPU units were not placed in secondary containment (see photo 5). However, the wells onsite were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. Soil conductivity readings were taken around the excavation, which read 2,360 and 2,750 Microsiemens (see photos 7 and 8). An additional conductivity reading was taken in what appeared to be a brine puddle at the bottom of the excavation, which read above the meter's range (see photo 9). A well tag was present on well 6H, with no observed leaks or discharge on the ground around it, and it appeared to be equipped for production (see photo 12). There are three other well heads onsite that also appear to be equipped for production (see photo 11). Production tanks were placed in secondary containment with no observed leaks with the containment (see photo 10). A rolloff dumpster was onsite that appeared to contain the impacted soil that was excavated (see photo 13). According to Mr. Crayne and Ms. Vallor-Bell, SPSI representatives will be onsite promptly to perform further cleanup and to cover the area of impact to prevent spread. Discussions are ongoing within EQT to determine how further remediation efforts will be conducted. Ms. Vallor-Bell stated that this spill will be remediated in accordance with Act 2. When it information is available, the Department requests that the operator provide the following information: - The quantity of what was spilled- How this quantity was obtained- How long was it on the ground- The last time the GPU and associated equipment was tended- Please include photos taken during remediation and the waste manifest

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/25/2024 to K PETROLEUM INC in Somerset Township, Washington county. 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/25/2024
Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8184781
Permit API: 125-22544
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: Somerset Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/25/2024
Comments: On April 25, 2024, inspection conducted at the US Natural Resources 1-P085 well site in Somerset Township, Washington County. This inspection follows up to IR 3744557, which documents the Department's response to a spill that reportedly occurred on April 10, 2024, when the onsite brine tank overfilled with production fluid and pushed a grease-like layer sitting on top of this fluid out the top of the tank onto the ground below. Present at this inspection were KPI representative Joel Grecko and myself. Mr. Grecko reports that remediation of the impacted area was completed on April 16, 2024. The following was observed:The access road appeared to be stable at the time of inspection with no observed evidence of accelerated erosion or sedimentation (see photo 1). Tire rutting was observed in the well site at the time of inspection (see photo 2). The area impacted by the grease-like substance was excavated with no staining observed in this area (see photo 3). No elevated soil conductivity was detected in this area, underneath the brine tank valve, or within the majority of the earthen berm surrounding the brine tank (see photos 4, 6, 7, 8, and 9). An area of slightly elevated conductivity was detected in the southwestern corner of the earthen berm surrounding the brine tank (see photos 5 and 9). However, no staining, distressed vegetation, or other visual impacts were observed in this area. The well head was equipped with a well tag, and no staining or distressed vegetation was observed on the ground around it (see photos 10 and 11). The operator's information was posted on the meter box (see photo 13). The brine tank appeared to be sound at the time of inspection, with any remaining grease-like substances appearing to have wiped off (see photo 14). Mr. Grecko was conducting brush clearing onsite when the Department arrived. Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends that maintenance is conducted on the well site (and on the access road, if needed) now that remediation is complete to address the aforementioned tire rutting. The Department recommends that the operator assess and evaluate the area of elevated conductivity in the earthen berm, as the conductivity reading taken in this location is an outlier when compared to other soil conductivity readings taken onsite. Finally the Department recommends that the remediated area is mulched and seeded until 70 percent vegetative growth coverage is achieved. The Department requests a response to this inspection report from the operator with the waste manifest from remediation included in this response, when available.Violations shall be noted and immediately corrected.
